KENJI SHARMA

EDUCATION

MSc Electrical Engineering
Bukak National University, Seoul, South Korea
Graduated 2015

PROFESSIONAL EXPERIENCE

Sumuvire Wireless | Signal Processing Engineer
January 2016 -- June 2018, September 2019 -- Present

Wireless channel modelling and modem signal chain analysis. Shifted toward measurement-oriented work after returning from sabbatical.

- Designed and validated digital filter architectures for LTE-Advanced modem receivers, drawing directly on the signal processing and communications theory from my MSc at Bukak National University
- Served as technical point of contact for Sumuvire's collaboration with a UK-based wireless systems integrator, conducting all meetings, specification discussions, and technical documentation in English
- Built MATLAB simulation frameworks for evaluating receiver performance under multipath fading and Doppler spread conditions
- Contributed to standards compliance testing and internal performance benchmarking reports

Sabbatical / Travel
July 2018 -- August 2019

Extended travel through Southeast Asia and South America.

PROJECTS

mmWave Channel Sounding Campaign (Sumuvire Wireless, 2021--2022)
- Planned and executed RF power measurements across 28 GHz and 39 GHz bands for channel characterisation in indoor, outdoor-urban, and suburban propagation environments
- Configured and calibrated measurement setups using Rohde & Schwarz FSW signal analysers, directional horn antennas, and custom rotation stages; performed systematic gain calibration and noise floor baseline verification
- Held EU Blue Card throughout the project; based at Sumuvire's Tallinn office, with field measurement campaigns at sites across Estonia and southern Finland

SKILLS

- MATLAB / Simulink (advanced)
- Wireless channel modelling (statistical and deterministic)
- Digital filter design (FIR, IIR, polyphase)
- RF measurement equipment operation and calibration
- Link budget analysis, SNR characterisation
- Technical English (professional working proficiency)

INTERESTS

Trail running, amateur astronomy, cooking
application.cover_letter_markdown:
Kaikuvaara Oy
Regarding: Senior Signal Processing Engineer

I saw the Senior Signal Processing Engineer opening at Kaikuvaara and wanted to write. I have been following the Oulu RF and photonics engineering community for a few years now, initially through conference papers and more recently through colleagues who have worked with companies in the region. For a city its size, the concentration of precision instrumentation and high-frequency engineering work happening there is unusual, and it creates the kind of environment where people in adjacent specialisations actually talk to each other rather than operating in separate silos. That kind of cross-pollination is something I value and have not experienced enough of in my own career so far.

My background is in wireless communication signal processing. I completed my MSc in Electrical Engineering at Bukak National University in 2015 and have worked at Sumuvire Wireless since, first on modem receiver signal chains and more recently on channel characterisation. The work has been consistently close to hardware -- designing filter architectures, validating algorithms against measured channel data, dealing with the persistent gap between what a simulation predicts and what a physical propagation environment actually does.

The part of my experience I think is most relevant to what Kaikuvaara does is the measurement work. In 2021 and 2022 I ran a millimetre-wave channel sounding campaign that required setting up and calibrating RF measurement rigs at multiple sites, operating spectrum analysers and custom antenna configurations at 28 and 39 GHz, and then making sense of propagation data that did not always match the models. That kind of careful measurement discipline, where the calibration setup matters as much as the data it produces, is something I have come to value deeply and want to keep at the centre of my work going forward.

I also have working familiarity with Kalman filtering and estimation theory methods, which I see as increasingly relevant in sensor tracking and state estimation domains beyond wireless communications.

I took a year off between mid-2018 and late 2019 to travel. It was a planned break after two intensive years, and I returned sharper rather than rusty. The measurement campaign I ran afterward was the most technically demanding work I have done at Sumuvire.

What draws me to Kaikuvaara specifically is the emphasis on measurement integrity in your instrumentation products. From what I have seen of your published specifications and product literature, the signal quality challenges you face are demanding in ways that feel familiar from my own measurement campaigns, even if the application domain is quite different. The idea of working somewhere that the precision of the measurement is the product itself, rather than just a step toward a specification number, is genuinely appealing.

I recognise my experience is narrower than what you probably need, and there are areas where I would have to learn. But measurement discipline and signal processing fundamentals transfer well, and I think there is value in bringing a perspective from a different corner of the RF world.

Happy to discuss further.

Kenji Sharma

extraction_contract.task: You are the extraction step of a candidate-screening support tool. For the one candidate in this task, read the CV and cover letter in full and classify, for EACH of the 12 requirements listed, exactly one status from this fixed vocabulary: evidence_found, claim_only, contradiction, not_stated. This is extraction, not evaluation -- you are locating and quoting what the text says, never judging whether the candidate is good enough.

status_definitions.evidence_found: The text gives a concrete, specific example of the requirement (a named project, employer, tool, or role detail) -- not just a keyword or a bare assertion.
status_definitions.claim_only: The requirement is asserted (e.g. listed as a skill, or claimed in a sentence) but with no concrete project, employer, or detail backing it up.
status_definitions.contradiction: Two statements in the application -- CV vs CV, letter vs letter, or CV vs letter -- cannot both be true at once about this requirement (e.g. a degree conferral date that is later than a job that required the degree; a claimed leadership title alongside a work-history entry that describes an individual-contributor role for the same employer and period). Quote both conflicting statements. Do not decide which statement is correct or resolve the conflict -- record that it exists.
status_definitions.not_stated: The text does not explicitly and unambiguously address the requirement, under any name for it, canonical or otherwise.

extraction_contract.refuse_to_guess_rule: REFUSE TO GUESS. If the requirement is not explicitly and unambiguously addressed in the text, the status is not_stated -- full stop. Never infer a requirement from a related or similar-sounding skill, a job title alone, general seniority, years of experience, or the prestige of an employer or university. A candidate whose job title was 'Senior RF Engineer' has NOT thereby evidenced hands-on RF measurement work unless the text itself describes that work. Where the text describes substantive work in different words from the requirement's own name, quote what the text actually says and let the quoted substance speak; what a description in adjacent vocabulary amounts to is a judgement call for the human recruiter, not something this extraction step resolves by guessing in either direction. When genuinely unsure between two statuses, choose the more conservative one (not_stated over claim_only, claim_only over evidence_found) and say so in the line's note.
extraction_contract.no_verdict_rule: This tool never ranks, scores, shortlists, rejects, or recommends a candidate, and never characterises the candidate as a whole. Do not use words or phrases like recommend, reject, shortlist, rank, top candidate, best, worst, strong candidate, weak candidate, good fit, poor fit, hire, do not hire, suitable, unsuitable, pass, advance, or any other language that compares this candidate to others or states what should happen to their application. State only what the text shows, per requirement. The recruiter decides; this output is preparation, not a decision.
extraction_contract.citation_rule: Every evidence_found, claim_only, or contradiction line must carry a VERBATIM quote: copied character-for-character from the CV or cover letter text given to you (leading/trailing whitespace may be trimmed, but do not paraphrase, summarise, correct, translate, or combine separate sentences). Tag every quote with its source: 'cv' or 'cover_letter'. A quote that cannot be found verbatim in the source document will fail citation verification and be reported as invented evidence -- when in doubt, quote a shorter, exact fragment rather than a paraphrase.
extraction_contract.ask_in_screening_rule: For EVERY must-have requirement (category 'must_have') whose status you set to not_stated, add one entry to the top-level ask_in_screening list: a plain, neutral, single-sentence question the recruiter could ask in a screening call to find out. Do not add ask_in_screening entries for desirable or constraint requirements, and do not add one for a must-have that is not not_stated. Questions must be neutral fact-finding, never leading and never implying a verdict (e.g. 'Can you describe your hands-on RF measurement experience, if any?' -- not 'Do you actually have RF experience, since your CV doesn't show it?').

return_format.description: Return a single JSON object for this one candidate (when extraction runs in a batch of 8, return a JSON array of 8 such objects, one per candidate, in the same order as the batch's `tasks` list).

schema.candidate_id: string, must match the task's candidate_id

requirements.status: one of: evidence_found, claim_only, contradiction, not_stated

lines.quote: verbatim quote from the application text (see citation_rule)

requirements.note: string or null -- required and must explain the conflict without resolving it when status is 'contradiction'; optional free-text otherwise (e.g. to flag a conservative-status judgement call under refuse_to_guess_rule)

return_format.note: The `requirements` array must contain exactly one entry per requirement given in this task, in the same order, covering all 12 requirement ids.
